inlines.v: REC'REATE, verb transitive [Latin recero; re and creo, to create.] 1. To refresh after toil; to reanimate, as languid spirits or exhausted strength; to amuse or divert in weariness. Painters when they work on white grounds, place before them colors mixed with blue and green, to recreate their eyes. St. John is said to have recreated himself with sporting with a tame partridge. 2. To gratify; to delight. These ripe fruits recreate the nostrils with their aromatic scent. 3. To relieve; to revive; as, to recreate the lungs with fresh air. REC'REATE, verb intransitive To take recreation.
